records.title: Completely unusable as a previous Halifax customer.
records.review:
Trying to migrate to the new Lloyds app from Halifax and I'm running into TWO bugs which are rendering the app unusable.

1.

When I open the Lloyds app it tells me to authenticate with Halifax and transfers to the Halifax app. In the Halifax app I approve the notification, which transfers me back to the Lloyds app. The Lloyds app then restarts the cycle and I’m stuck forever.

I’ve been through this cycle over 20 times and still can’t login to the Lloyds app. I've restarted both apps and my phone to no avail. 

2.

Later I tried again and it showed a different login screen, but then it wants to send me a code via phone call. Once I open the phone app to received the code the Lloyds app closes, and on returning it's gone back to the start and I have to restart the login flow, leaving me stuck in an infinite loop again!

Im on a new iPhone 17e, I actually had the same problem on on my 13 Pro which I just migrated from. I presume the app is being killed for excessive memory usage in the background but idk. I tried reporting it in the help chat back in the Halifax app but the virtual assistant was useless and the human support staff didn't mention if they reported the bug, so here I am. Please, fix your apps

records.title: Same Layout, Worse Experience
records.review:
I’ve just moved from the Halifax app over to Lloyds, and I’m genuinely surprised by how much harder I find it to use.

The layout is actually pretty similar, so I don’t think that’s the problem. It’s mainly the typography, spacing and colours. Everything feels much harder to scan at a glance, and the type in particular is really uncomfortable to read. After using Halifax for years, this honestly feels like a step backwards.

I know design is subjective, but for a banking app that people open all the time, readability and visual hierarchy really matter. I’d love to see the design and product teams put the Halifax and Lloyds apps side by side and compare how quickly you can actually find and read information.

It doesn’t need to look like Halifax, but it should at least feel as easy to use.
